newsitem.title: USA: Judge to ask bomb jury about subway attack.
newsitem.headline: Judge to ask bomb jury about subway attack.

text.p: A federal judge said on Friday he will ask jurors whether the spate of publicity generated by plans for an alleged New York subway attack will colour their judgment in the World Trade Centre bombing trial.

Lawyers for Ramzi Yousef, the accused mastermind of the bombing, and Eyad Ismoil, his co-defendant, told U.S. District Judge Kevin Duffy they were concerned that jurors may not be able to remain impartial because of widespread media attention about the bombing this week in Jerusalem and an alleged plot by three Middle Eastern men to blow up New York subways.
The judge said he would question each of the 12 permanent jurors and six alternates individually on Monday before the start of opening arguments in the case.

Yousef, the accused architect of the Feb. 26, 1993 bombing plot, and Ismoil are accused of planting a 1,200-pound (550 kg) fertiliser bomb at the WTC that killed six people, injured more than 1,000 and caused millions of dollars in damage.

The judge also refused to bar government scientific experts from testifying about chemical residue found during the extensive investigation. Defence lawyers wanted the testimony excluded after a highly publicised report by the Justice Department's inspector general last April criticised the FBI's crime laboratories' handling of the evidence.

Yousef was indicted in 1993 on charges of taking part in the trade centre car bombing, along with four other Moslem fundamentalists who were convicted in 1994 and sentenced to 240 years in prison each for their roles in the devastating explosion, which killed six people and injured hundreds.
Ismoil, a Jordanian, is accused of driving the van.

Prosecutors say Yousef -- who was born in Kuwait, holds an Iraqi passport but claims Pakistani and Palestinian ancestry -- fled the country to Karachi, Pakistan, hours after the explosion. He was arrested in Pakistan in February, 1995.

In September 1996, Yousef and two other radical Moslems were convicted of planning to bomb 12 U.S. passenger jets over the Pacific Ocean. He was also convicted of placing a bomb on a Philippine Airlines flight in 1994 as a trial run. The bomb killed a Japanese passenger and injured 10 others.
